desc: Build adjacency list from edges: for each `[u, v, w]`, add `(v, w)` to `u`'s list and `(u, w)` to `v`'s list.
`path_nodes`: list of node values in the current valid downward path.
`path_lens`: list of prefix sums of edge lengths from `path_nodes[0]` to each node in the path.
`last_pos`: dict mapping value → index in `path_nodes` of its last occurrence.

At each node: if `nums[node]` in `last_pos`, set `idx = last_pos[nums[node]]`, then trim `path_nodes` and `path_lens` to length `idx + 1` (keep nodes after the previous occurrence). Also remove any entries from `last_pos` whose indices are ≥ `idx+1` (or just ignore since we will re-add).
Append `nums[node]` to `path_nodes`; append new `path_lens` entry = `path_lens[-1] + edge_length_from_parent` (or `0` if root). Update `last_pos[nums[node]] = len(path_nodes) - 1`.
Current path length = `path_lens[-1]`, node count = `len(path_nodes)`. Update `best_len`/`best_nodes` accordingly.
Recurse on children (neighbors ≠ parent) passing the current edge length.
Backtrack: pop the last element from `path_nodes` and `path_lens`; delete `nums[node]` from `last_pos`.
Fix the code: remove the messy first implementation and the `break`, keep only the clean iterative DFS.
